EV031 and EV029 motivate the transferable proposal that donor/medium identity can alter intermediate populations or CO2-associated adduct chemistry, but they do not establish the same species in Co-bpy; this card therefore asks only whether TEA and TEOA produce different bounded vibrational signatures under otherwise matched conditions.","groups":[{"id":"E26G01","description":"Baseline operando run with TEOA under CO2 and light in the selected P01 formulation.","factors":[{"name":"platform","value":"P01 Co-bpy photocatalytic differences in reaction-state bands under matched conditions would support a substrate/intermediate-associated effect of TEA versus TEOA, but cannot by themselves distinguish adduct formation from altered cobalt state or medium effects."},{"group_a":"E26G01","group_b":"E26G03","changed_factors":["gas_isotope"],"inference":"Band shifts that track 13CO2 bound assignment to CO2-derived species; no shift argues against that assignment for those bands but not against all CO2-derived intermediates."},{"group_a":"E26G01","group_b":"E26G04","changed_factors":["solvent_isotope"],"inference":"Band shifts upon H2O to D2O substitution support involvement of exchangeable hydrogen in the assigned feature; absence of shift argues against that specific hydrogen-containing assignment."},{"group_a":"E26G01","group_b":"E26G05","changed_factors":["cobalt_component"],"inference":"Features present only when cobalt is included are more consistent with cobalt-associated reaction-state species; shared features indicate donor/support/background contributions and limit mechanistic assignment."}],"procedure":["Verify an IR-compatible reaction cell and establish a stable spectral baseline for the complete P01 medium before illumination, using the same optical path and gas handling for all groups.","Run matched illuminated CO2 experiments for TEA and TEOA, collecting time-resolved operando or near-operando IR spectra plus dark and cobalt-absent references under the same acquisition settings.","Repeat the TEOA condition with 13CO2 and, where spectral quality remains acceptable, with D2O substitution of the aqueous component to test isotope-sensitive assignments.","Process spectra by subtraction against appropriate pre-illumination and component-matched references, then compare emergence, shift, persistence, and decay of donor-dependent bands across groups.","Link any donor-dependent bands to parallel catalytic samples only descriptively, avoiding assignment of a full pathway unless isotope and control behavior are internally consistent."],"measurements":["Time-resolved IR spectra under illumination for all groups.","Wavenumber positions, isotope shifts, and temporal evolution of donor-dependent bands.","Presence or absence of candidate bands in cobalt-present versus cobalt-absent references.","Qualitative correspondence between operando spectral changes and separately measured CO/H2 outputs from matched catalytic runs.","Signal-to-noise, reproducibility across repeat runs, and extent of band overlap; these data cannot by themselves establish a unique intermediate structure or the rate-determining step."],"supports":"Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in reaction-state IR features under otherwise matched conditions, combined with isotope behavior that bounds at least one donor-dependent feature as CO2-derived and/or hydrogen-involving, and control behavior showing that the feature is not fully explained by donor-only background. This would support donor-specific substrate/intermediate stabilization or adduct-associated chemistry without proving a unique structure.","refutes":"Evidence against H05 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible donor-dependent reaction-state IR differences beyond baseline noise or generic medium effects, while isotope substitution fails to reveal bounded CO2-derived or hydrogen-sensitive features unique to one donor. That outcome would favor explanations centered elsewhere, such as quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes not visible here, or uncontrolled catalytic variability.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by overlap, weak signals, or baseline drift; if only multi-factor changes can be interpreted; if isotope substitution broadly perturbs the system without clear assignment value; or if donor-dependent bands appear but cannot be separated from cobalt-free or dark backgrounds. In that case the experiment remains descriptive and cannot discriminate H05 from competing explanations.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent literature conditions. Use the source-verified P01 formulation where available; otherwise first pilot the IR cell with the reported TEOA baseline to find the highest concentration/path length/collection time that preserves unsaturated absorbance and stable baselines. Keep reactor geometry, illumination, gas flow or headspace protocol, and acquisition timing identical across TEA and TEOA. Introduce 13CO2 and D2O only after confirming the baseline condition gives reproducible transient bands. If D2O causes major formulation instability or gross rate collapse, retain it as a bounded assignment aid rather than a matched mechanistic test.","limitations":"Transferred from non-Co systems and generic methods evidence. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, support, cobalt-ligand, bicarbonate/carbonate, and product bands can overlap. D2O and 13CO2 can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or that a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. The cobalt-absent control does not isolate support versus donor contributions separately.","feasibility":"specialist"}]}
